subject: pe

moments.title: First Laws of Cricket
moments.body: The Laws of Cricket are first codified in 1744. The Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC, founded 1787) becomes the custodian of the Laws — a role it still holds. The Laws (not rules — cricket is grand) have been continuously revised but never replaced.
moments.takeaway: Cricket has the oldest continuously codified ruleset of any major sport. The MCC, a private members' club, still owns the laws of an international sport.

moments.title: Bodyline series
moments.body: England's captain Douglas Jardine instructs fast bowlers (notably Harold Larwood) to bowl 'leg theory' — fast short-pitched deliveries aimed at the batsman's body — to neutralise Don Bradman. Australian batsmen are seriously injured. The Australian Cricket Board cables the MCC accusing 'unsportsmanlike' play. A diplomatic crisis between the UK and Australia ensues.
moments.takeaway: A cricket tactic almost ended commercial relations between the UK and Australia. The Laws were revised to outlaw bodyline.

moments.title: First T20 cricket
moments.body: The first professional Twenty20 (T20) match is played on 13 June 2003 — three hours, 20 overs per side. The format spreads rapidly. The Indian Premier League (2008) becomes the most lucrative T20 league. T20 transforms cricket's economics and athlete training.
moments.takeaway: A format invented for time-pressured English summer evenings became cricket's commercial centre within two decades.

now.title: Cricket today
now.body: Test cricket, ODIs and T20s coexist uneasily. The IPL pays the highest cricket salaries in history. The Hundred (ECB, 2021) attempted a further shorter format. Women's cricket has grown rapidly; the 2020 Women's T20 World Cup final at the MCG drew 86,174.
now.open_questions: Can Test cricket survive in an era of franchise T20 wealth? Player contracts increasingly favour franchise over national commitments.

reflection: Don Bradman's Test batting average of 99.94 is the most extreme statistical outlier in major sport. Bodyline was an England team's organised response to one batsman. Cricket is a team sport that has always orbited individuals.
